$comment: Both Nebraska local ordinances are carried as NOT IN EFFECT. They exist because LB 258 (2026) created a $13.50 youth and training wage below the state's $15.00, and both cities legislated to undo that locally; the state sued. An entry with a rate and no status field would be actively misleading here, so each carries an explicit status.

jurisdictions.name: Omaha
jurisdictions.status: enacted, not yet in effect, and under legal challenge
jurisdictions.coverage: Would restore a uniform $15.00 for all workers in Omaha, including those under 16 whom the state's LB 258 moved to a $13.50 youth wage.
jurisdictions.note: NOT IN EFFECT as of this file's asOf date (2026-09-08). The Omaha City Council passed the ordinance in July 2026 and the mayor signed it; it does not take effect until 2026-10-01, and the Nebraska Attorney General sued the city in August 2026 arguing the ordinance is unconstitutional. Until it takes effect and survives that challenge, Nebraska's state figures ($15.00 standard, $13.50 youth and training) are what Omaha employers owe -- which for most workers is the same number.

sources.title: Nebraska Attorney General -- suit against the City of Omaha over its minimum wage ordinance, and contemporaneous Omaha City Council coverage
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session across the Attorney General's own announcement and multiple independent news reports of the July 2026 council vote and mayoral signature.

jurisdictions.name: Lincoln
jurisdictions.coverage: Ordinance No. 21872 would have restored a uniform $15.00 and a CPI-U escalator effective 2026-07-18.
jurisdictions.note: NOT IN EFFECT. A Lancaster County District Court judge blocked Lincoln from enacting the ordinance on 2026-07-17, the day before it would have taken effect. Nebraska's state figures apply in Lincoln.

sources.title: Coverage of Lincoln Ordinance No. 21872 and the Lancaster County District Court order blocking it
sources.verifiedBy: cross_source_confirmed this session across independent Nebraska news reporting; the court order itself was not read.

sources.title: UC Berkeley Labor Center -- Inventory of US City and County Minimum Wage Ordinances
sources.verifiedBy: Fetched and read directly this session. The standing national census of local minimum wage ordinances -- used here to establish WHICH jurisdictions exist (so none is silently omitted), with each rate then cross-checked against a second source.

knownGaps: Both ordinances are in active litigation. This file records the position as of 2026-09-08 and will be wrong the moment a court rules or Omaha's 2026-10-01 date passes without an injunction -- re-verify before relying on either entry.
